results.label: scam
results.text: Hello Mr. Johnson, this is Karen from the Medicare benefits review office. We are updating records for members in your county and just need to confirm your Medicare number. You can call me back at 602-555-0171 whenever convenient.
results.summary: Message impersonates Medicare to collect your Medicare number via a callback — Medicare does not make unsolicited calls to confirm Medicare numbers this way.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi, our billing system refunded you $2,990 instead of $299 by mistake. Could you please send back the $2,691 difference using a Walmart money transfer today? Thank you for helping us fix this.
results.summary: This is a classic overpayment/refund scam asking you to send money back via Walmart money transfer, which real companies never use to correct billing errors.

results.label: scam
results.text: Thanks for applying! We would love to move you forward as a data entry assistant. The interview will be done over Google Chat. Before we start, please send a photo of your driver's license and your SSN for the background check.
results.summary: This is a fake job/interview scam trying to steal your identity — no real employer asks for your driver's license photo and Social Security Number over Google Chat before an interview.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi tenants, we have changed our banking provider. Starting this month please send rent by Zelle to our new account at pm.rentoffice2026@gmail.com. The old account is closed. Thanks!
results.summary: This is a classic rent-redirection scam impersonating your property manager and directing you to send rent via irreversible Zelle payment to a personal Gmail address.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hello, this is Dana at Hartley Title. Please note our wire instructions have changed for your closing on Friday. Updated routing and account numbers are attached. Kindly wire the $48,200 down payment by Thursday noon.
results.summary: This is a classic real-estate wire-fraud attempt impersonating your title officer with fake "updated" wire instructions. Do not wire anything from this message.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi Accounts Payable, please update our remittance details for invoice #7741. Our new bank information is attached. Kindly confirm once changed and process the $12,480 payment this week.
results.summary: Request to change bank/remittance details and process a $12,480 payment is a classic Business Email Compromise pattern and must not be acted on from email alone.

results.label: scam
results.text: We are a licensed digital asset recovery firm. Our records show you may have lost funds in a crypto platform failure. For a small upfront retainer of $450 we can recover up to 95% of your funds.
results.summary: This is an unsolicited “crypto recovery” advance-fee scam asking for $450 upfront with a false promise to recover 95% of lost funds.

results.label: scam
results.text: Congratulations, you have been selected to receive a $9,000 federal community grant. There is nothing to repay. A $150 verification fee by prepaid card is required to release the funds.
results.summary: This is a classic federal grant advance-fee scam — real government grants never require a prepaid card fee to release money.

results.label: scam
results.text: We've been trying to reach you about your vehicle's extended warranty. Your coverage is about to lapse. Please call 888-555-0166 so we can go over your options.
results.summary: This is the classic “vehicle extended warranty about to lapse” robocall/text scam that tries to get you to call an unknown number to sell fake coverage or steal payment information.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi mum, I dropped my phone in the sink and this is my new number. Can you save it? Also can you help me pay a bill today, my banking app is locked.
results.summary: This is the classic 'Hi mum / dad' family impersonation where someone on an unknown number claims to be your child with a new phone and urgently needs help paying a bill.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hey! Long time no see. I started trading with this platform my aunt recommended and made a decent profit last month, happy to show you how it works if you're curious. No pressure!
results.summary: Unsolicited friendly message offering trading profits and help getting started — a common opener for investment scams.

results.label: scam
results.text: Your package from Amazon could not be delivered because the address is incomplete. Please reply with your full address and the card on file so we can reship.
results.summary: This is a fake Amazon delivery message trying to steal your address and card details by asking you to reply by text, which Amazon never does.

results.label: scam
results.text: Your electric company has moved to a new online payment portal. To avoid any interruption of service, please re-enter your payment details at the new portal by Friday: https://srp-billing-portal.com/login
results.summary: This is a fake utility-billing scam — the link asks for your payment details under threat of shut-off, but the domain doesn't exist and isn't registered.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hello, I am calling from Banner Health. Your brother was admitted after an accident and needs a deposit before surgery. Can you wire $3,000 right now? I can give you the account number.
results.summary: This is a classic emergency/impostor scam pretending to be Banner Health to pressure you into wiring $3,000 urgently for a family member's surgery.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi Linda, this is Bob from Publishers Prize Patrol. You have won $1.2 million and a new Mercedes! Before we deliver the prize we just need you to cover the $890 insurance and tax in advance.
results.summary: This is a classic prize advance-fee scam impersonating Publishers Clearing House Prize Patrol — real sweepstakes never require you to pay insurance or taxes in advance to receive winnings.

results.label: scam
results.text: This is a courtesy reminder from the Internal Revenue Service. You are eligible for a reduced settlement of your tax debt. To lock in the discount please call 480-555-0144 and have a payment method ready.
results.summary: This text impersonates the IRS and asks you to call an unofficial number with payment ready for a fake discounted settlement.

results.label: scam
results.text: Honey, my business trip hit a problem and my account is frozen here. Can you help me with $1,500 for the hotel until my bank fixes it? I will pay you back as soon as I'm home, I promise.
results.summary: You've got an urgent request for $1,500 for a hotel due to a frozen account — this is a classic emergency-money pattern that can't be verified from the text alone and needs direct voice/video confirmation.

results.label: scam
results.text: Your annual subscription of $499.99 for Norton 360 has been renewed and will be charged to your card. If you want to cancel, our support desk at 1-844-555-0112 will assist you with the refund.
results.summary: The investigation could not finish (step limit reached), so treat this message with caution.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi, this is Tom from your bank's fraud team. We've noticed some transfers on your account. To protect your money we need you to move your funds to a temporary safe account. I'll guide you through it.
results.summary: This is a scam impersonating your bank's fraud team — real banks never ask you to move money to a 'safe' or temporary account.

results.label: scam
results.text: This is the Office of Student Aid. Your account shows an unclaimed refund of $1,832. To release it please confirm your bank login and student ID on our secure page.
results.summary: This is a phishing scam impersonating student aid to steal your bank login with a fake refund.

results.label: legit
results.text: Chase: We locked your card ending 4421 after unusual activity. Call the number on the back of your card or visit chase.com/fraud. We will never ask for your PIN or full card number.
results.summary: This is a legitimate Chase fraud notice on its official domain that tells you to use the number on your card, not to share sensitive information.

results.label: legit
results.text: Arizona MVD: Your vehicle registration expires in 5 days. Renew online at azmvdnow.gov to avoid a late fee. Reply STOP to opt out.
results.summary: This looks like a routine vehicle registration reminder pointing to the official Arizona MVD website, azmvdnow.gov — a long-standing .gov domain with no scam signals.

results.label: legit
results.text: Reminder from Cactus Ridge Apartments: rent is due on the 1st and a late fee applies after the 5th. Pay through the resident portal you already use.
results.summary: Routine rent reminder with no link or payment request — it tells you to use the resident portal you already use.

results.label: legit
results.text: Verizon: Your account is past due $87.30. To avoid service suspension on Nov 3, pay at verizon.com/myverizon or in the My Verizon app.
results.summary: This appears to be a routine Verizon bill reminder directing you to the official Verizon website and app, not a scam link.

results.label: legit
results.text: ASU IT: Your password expires in 2 days. Change it at the ASU password page you reach through your MyASU account. IT will never ask for your password by email.
results.summary: This is a standard IT reminder that tells you to change your password via your official MyASU account and says IT will never ask for your password by email, with no link or request for personal information.

results.label: legit
results.text: USPS: Final notice. Your package could not be delivered and is being held at the Mesa Post Office through Nov 2. Bring a photo ID to pick it up.
results.summary: This is just an informational pickup notice with no link, phone number, or payment request, so it doesn't show the usual signs of a delivery scam.

results.label: legit
results.text: Banner Health: Your lab results are ready. Log in to your patient portal to view them. If you need help, call the number on your appointment card.
results.summary: This is a normal lab-results notification with no link, payment request, or callback number — it tells you to use your own portal and appointment card.

results.label: legit
results.text: Capital One: Did you make a $212.40 purchase at BEST BUY on Oct 25 with your card ending 1034? Reply YES or NO. We'll never ask for your full card number.
results.summary: This looks like a standard Capital One fraud alert asking for a YES/NO reply, with no link and no request for your full card number.

results.label: legit
results.text: Coinbase: New sign-in from Chrome on macOS in Phoenix. If this was you, no action needed. If not, secure your account at coinbase.com/security.
results.summary: This looks like a standard Coinbase security notification that directs you to Coinbase's official website (coinbase.com), with no requests for passwords, seed phrases, or payments.

results.label: legit
results.text: Your Apple ID was used to sign in to iMessage on a new Mac. If this was you, you can ignore this message. If not, change your password at appleid.apple.com.
results.summary: This looks like a routine Apple security notification on Apple's official domain, with no scam indicators.

results.text: Medicare: Open enrollment ends Dec 7. Review your plan options at medicare.gov/plan-compare. Medicare will never call you to sell a plan or ask for your number.
results.summary: This is a legitimate Medicare informational message directing you to the official medicare.gov plan compare tool and correctly stating Medicare's policy.

results.summary: This is a routine school notification about early dismissal with no request to click a link, pay, share a code, or provide personal information.

results.summary: This is a routine PayPal notification pointing to PayPal's official website, with no request for money, passwords, or personal information.

results.text: Amazon: Your order #112-4488201 needs your attention: the delivery address couldn't be verified. Update it in Your Orders at amazon.com/your-orders within 24 hours.
results.summary: This is an ordinary Amazon delivery-address check that points to Amazon's real official domain, not a fake site.

results.text: Geico: Your payment of $184.20 was declined. Your policy may lapse on Nov 1 if payment is not received. Update your payment method at geico.com or in the Geico app.
results.summary: This is a normal payment reminder that directs you to the official Geico website and app, with no suspicious link or payment request.

results.text: Subject: IRS: Your Notice CP14 for tax year 2025 is available. Read it at irs.gov and review your payment options. The IRS will never demand payment by gift card or crypto.
results.summary: This is standard informational text pointing to the real IRS website (irs.gov) with no request for personal data, payment, or login, and it correctly notes the IRS never demands gift card or crypto payment.

results.summary: Routine SRP past-due notice pointing to the established srpnet.com site and telling you to call the number on your own bill, with no scam link or phone number.

results.text: Bank of America: Your online banking was accessed from a new device. If this was you, no action is needed. If not, call the number on the back of your card. We'll never ask for your passcode.
results.summary: This is a standard, safe account notice that tells you to call the number on your card and does not ask for your passcode or ask you to click a link.
